what_happened: The person running Athena re-queued the stand-in-script (ETXTBSY) flaky-test fix for a third time. Two earlier tries were rejected because a source-scan test that the reader added to the reading missed cases. This time the request limits the work to the child-process helper and the call sites converted to use it, and it leaves out any source-scan test. No job failed in this event. It is an intervention where the the person running Athena gave the method and the scope.
cause: Athena accepts a bug request for an intermittent failure without requiring the root mechanism to be named. It also lets the reading invent a proof method, here a source scan, with no check that the method can actually show coverage. A scan over source text cannot tell which paths really trigger the failure, so it misses cases, and the verifier rejects the job for that. Because the failure is intermittent, a passing run proves nothing, so the verifier can neither confirm nor rule out a fix. Nothing carried forward what earlier attempts left uncovered or why a verification approach failed. The the person running Athena's knowledge of the mechanism (inherited write handles) and of which proof to leave out was again the only source of the design.
prevention: Require a bug job for an intermittent failure to name the root mechanism before any code is written. Record a coverage claim that lists every path that can trigger the mechanism, including paths in production code that tests reach only indirectly. Check it by routing all such paths through one shared helper whose use is enforced by a test on the helper's behavior, not by a text scan. When a retry follows a rejection, carry the earlier findings into the reading, including which proof approaches failed and why. Have the reading take its scope from the rejected attempts and not invent new criteria. After two rejections for the same cause, stop and require a stated root cause before a third attempt.
proposed_request: Fix the intermittent ETXTBSY ("text file busy") failures in tests that write stand-in scripts and then run them. Cause: the parent process holds an inherited write handle open while another process executes the file. Outcome: every stand-in script in the test suite is written through one shared helper that writes the file from a child process, so the parent never holds a write handle on a script that is about to run. Scope: add that helper and convert the call sites that write and then run stand-in scripts, including any in production code that tests reach. Acceptance: (1) the helper exists and has a test that writes a script through it and runs it immediately, repeated many times with no ETXTBSY; (2) each converted call site uses the helper and no longer writes the script directly; (3) the existing test suite passes. Do not add a source-scan test that searches the code for direct writes, because two earlier attempts were rejected when such a scan missed cases. Change nothing outside the helper and the converted call sites.
